area: AREA 1: setup description faults (G-LIGHT deferrals + cast/creature names leaking from setup described/geometry into every take)
summary: Two faults share one leak path: setup.described/geometry text is pasted verbatim into every grid cell (studio/storyboard_grid.py place_clause, line 72-76) and every take prompt (scripts/episode/takes_r2v.py:512), so a person or bare creature named there is drawn as a phantom in EVERY take of that setup, and a described without a directional light flattens every frame. The existing G-LIGHT checker (house_style.setup_faults) and mechanical cure (plan_cures.light_directions) are both correct but disconnected: plan_check.py:200 prints the fault list as a one-line repr that plan_repair.fault_rows (which collects only 4-space-indented rows) never sees, so the cure never dispatched and the writer deferred — the exact fixture in tests/test_the_cure_measures_like_the_checker.py:62 asserts a stdout format the checker does not emit. Design: (1) fix the G-LIGHT print to indented rows so the existing cure fires; (2) add a new hard gate G-PHANTOM in studio/plan_gates.py that refuses any sentence of a setup's described/geometry naming a cast token (from refs.json rows, creatures included via gender=="creature"), a generic person noun, or a bare creature word; (3) a mechanical cure strip_phantoms that deletes the offending sentence exactly as Claude did, guarded so the setup stays at/above the G-FIRSTFRAME per-setup floors (DESCRIBED_WORDS=90 / GEOMETRY_WORDS=60, plan_gates.py:59-65), and a workhorse-tier llm cure rewrite_setups (through studio/llm.structured, guard_spend automatic in _NativeStructuredCaller._parse, line 184) for setups where deletion would breach the floor or where no light source exists to anchor the mechanical clause; (4) one PICTURE_RULES line so the writer stops producing and stops re-adding these on re-sign — the re-add is also structurally dead because every write_plan lapses the sha8-bound plan.verdict.json and the battery re-fires G-PHANTOM.

gates.where: studio/plan_gates.py — new functions appended after close_crowd_faults (line 457): PERSON_NOUN regex, person_tokens(refs), phantom_hits(text, names, place_words), phantom_faults(episode, names, place_words). Wired into scripts/episode/plan_check.py main() right after the G-CROWD-CLOSE block (after line 218): hoist the refs.json read currently at line 239 up to just after line 201, build names = plan_gates.person_tokens(refs) and place_words = house_style.place_words(), then print('G-PHANTOM    :', len(pf) or 'clean'); for f in pf: print('   ', f[:170]); hard += len(pf)
gates.rule: For every setup, for each field in ('described','geometry') — never 'crowd', which legitimately stages people and has its own gates — split into sentences on r'(?<=[.!?])\s+'; a sentence is refused when it contains (a) any token from person_tokens: plan_gates.cast_tokens (line 369) run over every refs.json character row's entity_id PLUS its display-name words, creatures included (rows with gender=='creature' cover 'Martian'), matched case-insensitively at word boundaries including possessives (token + r"(?:'s)?"); or (b) PERSON_NOUN = re.compile(r"\b(?:man|men|woman|women|people|person|persons|figure|figures|child|children|boy|boys|girl|girls|crowd|onlookers?|bystanders?)\b", re.I); exception: a hit whose token also appears in house_style.place_words() (a place name like St John's Wood) is skipped. Fault row format: fault('G-PHANTOM', f"setup {name!r} ({field})", f"sentence {sent[:50]!r} names {token!r}; a place description is the empty stage and this sentence prints a phantom into every take of the setup", 1, 0). Each gate helper 10-20 lines, one job.

Replace print('G-LIGHT      :', unlit or 'clean') with print('G-LIGHT      :', len(unlit) or 'clean') followed by for f in unlit: print('   ', f[:170]) — the same indented-row shape PLAN GATES uses at line 206-207. This is what lets plan_repair.fault_rows collect G-LIGHT rows and dispatch the already-written light_directions cure (CURES line 330). Without it the whole G-LIGHT cure chain is dead code, which is the measured root cause of the ep18 deferral.

cures.fault: G-PHANTOM: a setup described/geometry sentence names a cast member, creature, or generic person noun
cures.how: studio/plan_cures.py: strip_phantoms(doc, names, place_words) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]. For each setup and field, recompute phantom hits with the gate's own phantom_hits (import from plan_gates — the cure MEASURES LIKE THE CHECKER, the house rule plan_cures.py:204-206 states); delete each offending sentence (re-split, drop, rejoin with single spaces) EXACTLY as Claude did by hand, but only commit the deletion when the field's remaining word count stays >= its G-FIRSTFRAME per-setup floor (plan_gates.DESCRIBED_WORDS=90 for described, plan_gates.GEOMETRY_WORDS=60 for geometry — a conservative per-setup bound that guarantees the plan MEDIAN floor holds). When deletion would breach the floor, leave the field untouched and append the setup name to the returned residue list for the llm cure. Dispatcher wiring: add (re.compile(r'G-PHANTOM'), 'strip_phantoms') to CURES (insert next to the G-CROWD-CLOSE row, line 334); add the 'strip_phantoms' elif branch in scripts/episode/plan_repair.py apply() (after the close_crowds branch, line 94-95), building names/place_words inside apply() from book/'refs'/'refs.json' (guarded by .exists()) and house_style.place_words(). Cost $0.

cures.fault: G-PHANTOM residue (deletion would breach the word floor) and G-LIGHT residue (described names no light-source noun at all, so light_directions' default 'Raking grey daylight from the LEFT' clause has nothing in the setup's own words to anchor)
cures.how: studio/plan_cures.py: SetupRewrite(BaseModel): described: str; geometry: str. rewrite_setups(doc, names, place_words, setup_names, caller=None): one call per setup through studio.llm.structured('workhorse', PHANTOM_PROMPT.format(...), SetupRewrite, _agent=caller) — the _agent seam (llm.py:269) is the FakeModel injection point, guard_spend fires automatically inside _NativeStructuredCaller._parse (llm.py:184) against money.episode_ceiling_usd=$3, and StructuredOutputException retry (retries=3 with re_ask) is llm.structured's own ladder. After each call, validate IN CODE: plan_gates.phantom_hits(result.described, names, place_words)==[] and same for geometry, plan_cures.has_light_direction(result.described) True, word floors held (>=90/>=60); on validation failure re-ask once with the failure appended via llm.re_ask, then on second failure keep the original field and leave the fault row standing (it exits plan_repair as a CREATIVE row for the writer — default ESCALATE posture for anything judgement could not settle). Dispatch point: scripts/episode/plan_repair.py main(), after the mechanical ROUNDS loop ends with faults remaining (between lines 134 and 135): collect rows matching r'G-PHANTOM|G-LIGHT: setup', derive setup names via re.search(r"setup '([^']+)'", row), call pc.rewrite_setups once (never in the per-round loop — at most one paid round per repair run, at most MAX_SETUPS calls), write through episode_home.write_plan (contract-validated, lapses the sha8-bound plan.verdict.json), re-run battery_rows. Estimated spend: ~1.8k prompt + ~500 output tokens per setup on the workhorse tier; <=$0.01/setup, <=~$0.06/episode worst case — guard_spend refuses before sending if the $3 ceiling would be crossed.
cures.prompt_template:
You are rewriting ONE setup description for a storyboard pipeline.
Every sentence below is pasted verbatim into every image prompt of this place, so any person or
creature it names is DRAWN into every frame of every shot as a phantom extra.

SETUP: {name}

DESCRIBED (current):
{described}

GEOMETRY (current):
{geometry}

Rewrite both fields under these rules:
1. Remove every mention of a person or creature. Banned names and their possessive forms: {banned}.
   Also banned as bare words: man, men, woman, women, people, person, figure, figures, child,
   children, boy, girl, crowd, onlooker, bystander.
   Keep what each such sentence says about the PLACE itself: 'The narrator and the curate approach
   along the dusted roadway' becomes 'The dusted roadway runs toward the gate, dust lying thick on it.'
2. Keep every object, surface, distance and frame-edge placement already present. Invent no new objects.
3. DESCRIBED must name one light source WITH a direction — a practical (lamp, fire, window, doorway)
   or sky light plus where it falls from, e.g. 'Grey daylight comes from the LEFT, low from the west'
   or 'A low fire burns in the hearth, deep shadow beyond it.' A brightness alone ('hard morning
   sunlight') is refused, and an overhead sun is refused.
4. DESCRIBED stays at or above {described_floor} words and GEOMETRY at or above {geometry_floor} words;
   reach the floor by describing the place's fixed things, never by naming people.
5. Plain declarative present-tense sentences. No camera words, no story events, no sound.
Return both rewritten fields in full.

risks: False positives from short or common cast tokens: cast_tokens already drops tokens <=2 chars and non-unique tokens, and the place_words() exclusion covers place-name collisions (e.g. 'john' in St John's Wood), but a cast member named after a common object word (e.g. an id token like 'wells' or 'green') could still refuse an innocent setup sentence; the llm cure then rewrites a sentence that was fine — cheap, but it churns prose. Mitigate by logging every G-PHANTOM hit with its sentence so the next calibration pass can add an allowlist.

The per-setup floor guard (>=90/>=60 words after deletion) is stricter than the gate's MEDIAN floor, so some deletions that the median would tolerate get routed to the paid llm cure instead — a few cents of unnecessary spend, never a wrong plan.

The llm rewrite may drop a geometry relation the grids depended on despite rule 2; the storyboard cell gates (cell_gates) downstream still check cells against the plan, and the plan diff is visible in git since write_plan rewrites plan.json in place on a signed-off tree.

Changing the G-LIGHT print format: any other consumer parsing plan_check stdout for the old one-line list (grep found only plan_repair.fault_rows and the drifted test fixture, but a shell script outside the repo could exist) would need the same one-line fix.

Writer re-adding on re-sign is contained, not prevented: the battery+cure loop will strip the sentence again each round; if the writer re-adds in the same round as a creative fix, plan_repair converges only because strip_phantoms is idempotent — the PICTURE_RULES line is the actual prevention and its effect should be measured on the next episode's deferral count.
